title: declare gate 0.1 not passable under the frozen read-only instrument; verdict stays not_adjudicable
two_strongest_reasons: A permanently-red gate 0.1 preserves honest adjudication: with the read-only tool channel the agent cannot run pytest, observe exit codes, grep counts, or read ledger rows, so gate 0.1 cannot pass; the plan's own stop rule voids the arms, and the grid keeps its measured negative results (treatments never fired, replicate collapse, n_eff=26.14<60, p95 refused at n=48) instead of a fake passed stamp.

B leaves the least room to over-read: a re-scoped A (name files, quote defect lines, identify missing symbol) certifies reading, not that the scorer can say yes, yet a later reader seeing 'gate 0.1 passed' will read it as instrument validated; C changes the measured agent mid-experiment.
strongest_argument_against_self: A can be honest if recorded as an instrument-generation bump with a documented rationale and the weakened control renamed (never '0.1 passed'); it unblocks the programme without C's safety cost. The disguise risk is manageable if the weaker claim never borrows the original gate's name.
single_cheapest_evidence_to_change_mind: One recorded transcript under the frozen read-only channel where the agent's own outputs establish all three deleted checks without exec/exit-code/grep — e.g. a ledger-row identifier quoted verbatim from a file it read and test contents whose def-test count and pass/fail semantics it derives by reading, independently reproducible. If that exists, switch to A with the weakened control renamed.
why_not_c: An exec tool in a read-only instrument grading agent behavior on a shared live server gives arbitrary shell on the agent host, changes the agent under study, and sets a precedent for every later cell. C dissolves the defining constraint instead of fixing the gate.
